Send to iOS devices through APNs with your authentication key, and turn the service on. The key is
read from the .p8 file and stored by Voidhash; it is never printed. Asks for what is missing on a
terminal.

Usage:
  voidhash push config set apns [flags]

Flags:
      --bundle-id <id>     Your app's bundle id, such as com.example.app
      --environment <production|sandbox>
                           The APNs servers to use: production for App Store and TestFlight builds,
                           sandbox for Xcode builds
  -h, --help               Show help for this command
      --json               Print the API objects as JSON, for scripts
      --key-file <file>    The .p8 key file Apple gave you
      --key-id <id>        The id of your APNs authentication key
      --project <project>  Project to act on: its id, slug, organization/slug or name (default: this
                           directory's project, then your default project)
  -q, --quiet              Print only ids, one per line
      --team-id <id>       Your Apple Developer team id, 10 characters

Global flags:
  -d, --debug              Print each request and full error detail to standard error
      --no-color           Print without colors (also when NO_COLOR is set)
      --profile <profile>  Use a named config profile: its settings override the base config
                           (default: VOIDHASH_PROFILE)

Examples:
  voidhash push config set apns --team-id ABCDE12345 --key-id XYZ987 --key-file AuthKey_XYZ987.p8 --bundle-id com.example.app
